findings.title: Preserve right-aligned controls in the small-action flex layout
findings.body: The new flex layout leaves `.small-action-desc` content-sized because it has no positive flex-grow, while action buttons still rely on `float: right`. That float cannot preserve right-edge placement: it is ignored on direct flex children, and buttons inside the description can only float to the edge of its now-narrow box. Short action notices therefore pull their controls next to the notice instead of keeping them at the row's right edge. Make the description consume the remaining space and use flex-aware positioning for the controls.

findings.title: Preserve panel positioning in the legacy flexbox fallback
findings.body: Browsers using the newly emitted `display: -webkit-box` fallback, such as the Android 4.3 stock browser, do not distribute remaining space through auto margins in that box model. With `float: right` removed and no preceding item assigned `-webkit-box-flex: 1`, the header panel is packed immediately after the logo/topic information rather than against the right edge. The legacy fallback needs a flexible preceding item or another compatible right-alignment mechanism.

findings.title: Include alignment for the Mozilla box fallback
findings.body: The display mixins emit `-moz-box` and `-moz-inline-box`, but the alignment mixin omits `-moz-box-align`. Firefox versions using those legacy display values ignore all the emitted alignment properties and retain the default stretch alignment. In particular, switching bullet badges from their inline-block fallback to `-moz-inline-box` now loses the intended baseline alignment between the category marker and its text. Emit the matching Mozilla alignment property.
